title: Unit – 2 : Session – 8 | Harmony in Family and Society — Hiware Bazar
sections: Q1. Hiware Bazar's GOAL: a prosperous, harmonious and self-reliant village — continuous happiness and prosperity for ALL families, not just a few. PROGRAM: collective decision-making (gram sabha), water conservation and watershed development, ban on liquor, planned cropping suited to water availability, shared labour (shramdan), education and health for all — i.e., right understanding applied to relationship within the village and to work with nature, reversing migration and scarcity.

Q2. INTEGRATED family/society: members share a common goal, take decisions together, trust one another, and individual effort supports the collective — prosperity of one adds to all. FRAGMENTED family/society: each member/family pursues private accumulation, decisions are contested, trust is absent, and one family's gain is seen as another's loss — resources may exist yet conflict and scarcity-feeling persist. Integration is a function of shared feeling and understanding, not of wealth.

Q3. The two questions about physical facility: (1) 'Physical facility for WHAT?' — what is its purpose, whom does it serve? (2) 'How MUCH is enough?' — has the need been assessed? The deeper point: money is only a MEANS; without right understanding of its purpose and sufficiency, rising income funds liquor, gambling, show-off and conflict — misuse rises with income. Prosperity requires the feeling of sufficiency and right utilisation, not merely more money.

Q4. Four indicators of a humane society: (1) RIGHT UNDERSTANDING in every individual — measures how many live with clarity of human goals; (2) PROSPERITY in every family — measures whether each family has the feeling and reality of more-than-required facility; (3) FEARLESSNESS (trust) in society — measures whether people live without fear of one another; (4) CO-EXISTENCE with nature — measures whether production and consumption enrich rather than degrade the rest of nature.

Q5. REFLECTION on my family: our stated goal is comfort and education; the program is mostly individual effort — each member busy with own work/study, joint decisions occasional. Compared to Hiware Bazar, we lack a SHARED goal discussed together and collective responsibility beyond the household. Improvement: a regular family dialogue to define our common goal (happiness and prosperity of all members + contribution to society), assessment of our real needs, and participation of every member in decisions — moving from a merely co-existing family to an integrated one.
